entries.subject: Celestia native nucleus illustration and catalog scale
entries.finding: Superseded 2026-09-16: the Celestia generic mesh was a shared illustration with no relation to this nucleus, and its catalogue radius was an estimate. The package now shows a smooth ellipsoid at the published effective radius (Liu, Hui and Liu (2025), A&A 698, A95); no mesh from Celestia is retained.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured shape model of this nucleus (radar, spacecraft or a convex lightcurve inversion with a stated pole) would replace the ellipsoid.

entries.subject: Object-specific measured shape in PDS/Stooke archives
entries.finding: The retained catalog intake names the Stooke archive but contains no object-specific mesh search result or inspected reconstruction for this comet. The Celestia illustration is selected; the record does not establish that a measured shape is unavailable.
entries.revisitWhen: An object-specific archive product or published numerical shape can be inspected, with coordinates, scale and reuse terms.

entries.subject: Published event and observation context
entries.finding: Retained intake decision: Tsuchinshan–ATLAS became a bright evening comet in October 2024. Its tail stretched across SOHO’s field of view as it passed near the Sun. The cited material supplies explanatory context; it does not qualify photographic terrain on this nucleus.

entries.subject: Cited context observations as a nucleus surface texture
entries.finding: The retained intake did not establish resolved nucleus pixels, camera-to-shape registration or a surface coverage mask for these context observations. They are not used as surface texels. This decision concerns the cited material, not every observation of the comet.
entries.revisitWhen: A resolved nucleus image with usable geometry and an independently checked mapping to a source shape becomes available.

entries.subject: Published effective nucleus radius
entries.finding: Liu, Hui and Liu (2025), A&A 698, A95: effective radius 5.9 km. Only an upper limit is published; the nucleus is displayed at that limit as a sphere and may be smaller. Used as the volume-equivalent radius of the displayed ellipsoid.
